description: Programmatic control of notebooks and cells from the kernel: notebook and cell objects, reading and writing selections, finding and evaluating cells, saving and closing notebooks, front-end tokens, cell styles and tags, notebook templates, and window creation.

tools.name: NotebookObject
tools.description: NotebookObject[fe, id] represents an open notebook in the front end; it is returned by CreateDocument, NotebookOpen, EvaluationNotebook[], InputNotebook[], SelectedNotebook[] and Notebooks[]. All notebook manipulation functions take it as their first argument; Options[nb] and SetOptions[nb, ...] read and change notebook options such as WindowTitle.
tools.usage:
nb = EvaluationNotebook[]
nb = InputNotebook[]
nb = SelectedNotebook[]
Notebooks[]
Notebooks["title"]
SetOptions[nb, WindowTitle -> "Results"]
tools.example:
nb = EvaluationNotebook[];
Options[nb, WindowTitle]
NotebookFileName[nb]
NotebookInformation[nb]
tools.notes: EvaluationNotebook[] is the notebook containing the evaluating cell; InputNotebook[] the one that would receive typed input; SelectedNotebook[] the frontmost window. These differ during palette-driven or background evaluations.

tools.name: NotebookOpen
tools.description: Opens a notebook file in the front end and returns its NotebookObject (Visible -> False opens it hidden for batch processing). NotebookSave writes it back (optionally to a new path), NotebookClose closes it. Together they form the open-process-save loop for batch editing of notebooks.
tools.usage:
nb = NotebookOpen["file.nb"]
nb = NotebookOpen["file.nb", Visible -> False]
NotebookSave[nb]
NotebookSave[nb, "new.nb"]
NotebookClose[nb]
tools.notes: Requires a front end (UsingFrontEnd in wolframscript). For headless work without a front end, Get/Import of the .nb expression and Export are alternatives.

tools.name: NotebookGet
tools.description: Returns the complete Notebook[{Cell[...], ...}, opts] expression of an open notebook, the counterpart of NotebookPut. Use it to analyse or transform a notebook as data (extract inputs, rewrite styles) before writing it back.
tools.usage:
NotebookGet[nb]
NotebookGet[]

tools.name: NotebookRead
tools.description: Reads the expression corresponding to the current selection in a notebook (or to a given CellObject / BoxObject) back into the kernel. Combine with SelectionMove to walk through a notebook cell by cell.
tools.usage:
NotebookRead[nb]
NotebookRead[cellObject]
NotebookRead[{cell1, cell2, ...}]

tools.name: SelectionMove
tools.description: Moves the selection in a notebook: direction Next, Previous, Before, After, All and unit Cell, CellGroup, CellContents, Character, Word, Expression, Notebook. It is the cursor-positioning primitive underlying NotebookWrite, NotebookRead and NotebookDelete workflows.
tools.usage:
SelectionMove[nb, dir, unit]
SelectionMove[nb, dir, unit, n]
SelectionMove[cellObject, dir, unit]
SelectionMove[nb, After, Notebook]

parameters.name: unit
parameters.description: Cell, CellGroup, CellContents, Character, Word, Expression, Notebook.

parameters.name: AutoScroll
parameters.description: Option: scroll to the new selection.

tools.name: NotebookFind
tools.description: Searches a notebook for text, cell tags, cell styles or cell labels (forward or backward) and selects the first match, returning $Failed if none. Use it with NotebookRead/NotebookDelete to locate and edit specific cells.
tools.usage:
NotebookFind[nb, "text"]
NotebookFind[nb, "text", Next]
NotebookFind[nb, "tag", All, CellTags]
NotebookFind[nb, "Section", Next, CellStyle]

tools.name: NotebookDelete
tools.description: Deletes the current selection in a notebook, or the given CellObject(s) or a TemporaryCell returned by PrintTemporary. Use it to remove generated output, clear sections before regenerating a report, or dismiss attached cells.
tools.usage:
NotebookDelete[nb]
NotebookDelete[cellObject]
NotebookDelete[{cell1, cell2, ...}]

parameters.name: nb / cellObject
parameters.description: Notebook whose selection is deleted, or specific cells.

tools.example:
NotebookDelete[Cells[nb, CellStyle -> "Output"]] (* delete all outputs *)
NotebookDelete[Cells[nb, CellTags -> "generated"]]

tools.name: Cells
tools.description: Returns the list of CellObjects in a notebook (or cell group), optionally filtered by CellStyle, CellTags, CellID, CellLabel or GeneratedCell. It is the query function for cell-level notebook manipulation; each CellObject can be read, deleted, styled with SetOptions, or evaluated.
tools.usage:
Cells[]
Cells[nb]
Cells[nb, CellStyle -> "Input"]
Cells[nb, CellTags -> "tag"]
Cells[cellGroupObject]

tools.name: CellObject
tools.description: CellObject[id] refers to a specific cell in an open notebook; obtained from Cells, SelectedCells, EvaluationCell, PreviousCell, NextCell, ParentCell or CellPrint. Supports Options/SetOptions (cell-level options such as CellTags, Background, Editable), NotebookRead, NotebookDelete and SelectionMove.
tools.usage:
EvaluationCell[]
SelectedCells[nb]
PreviousCell[cell]
NextCell[cell]
ParentCell[cell]
SetOptions[cell, CellTags -> {"tag"}]
Options[cell, CellStyle]

tools.name: SelectionEvaluate
tools.description: Evaluates the currently selected cells in a notebook (like pressing Shift+Enter), optionally moving the selection afterwards; SelectionEvaluateCreateCell creates a new cell for the result. Use it in automation that steps through cells or in palette buttons that evaluate the user's selection.
tools.usage:
SelectionEvaluate[nb]
SelectionEvaluate[nb, sel]
SelectionEvaluateCreateCell[nb]
tools.notes: NotebookEvaluate evaluates a whole notebook (optionally hidden) without touching the selection.

tools.name: NotebookApply
tools.description: Writes data into a notebook at the current selection, replacing the selection placeholder (■) inside the inserted expression with the previously selected content. Used by palette buttons that wrap the user's selection in a function, e.g. Simplify[■].
tools.usage:
NotebookApply[nb, data]
NotebookApply[nb, data, sel]

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Boxes or string containing the selection placeholder \[SelectionPlaceholder].

tools.name: NotebookLocate
tools.description: Finds cells with a given cell tag (in the input notebook or in a file/URL) and scrolls/selects them - the mechanism behind hyperlinks that jump within notebooks. Use it to implement navigation in generated documents.
tools.usage:
NotebookLocate["tag"]
NotebookLocate[{"file.nb", "tag"}]

tools.name: CellTags
tools.description: Option of Cell holding a list of string tags used to locate cells (NotebookFind, NotebookLocate, Cells[..., CellTags -> ...]) and to select cells for export or evaluation. CellLabel is the visible In[n]/Out[n] label, CellID a unique integer id, and CellStyle the style name used in Cells filters.
tools.usage:
Cell[..., CellTags -> {"tag1", "tag2"}]
Cells[nb, CellTags -> "tag1"]
SetOptions[cell, CellTags -> {"tag"}]

tools.name: CellStyle
tools.description: Filter key for Cells and NotebookFind selecting cells by style name ("Input", "Output", "Text", "Section", "Code", ...). Styles are defined in the notebook's stylesheet (StyleDefinitions option); Cell[content, "Style"] assigns one. Use it to process only certain cell types.
tools.usage:
Cells[nb, CellStyle -> "Section"]
NotebookFind[nb, "Code", All, CellStyle]
Cell["heading", "Section"]

tools.name: NotebookImport
tools.description: Imports the cells of a given style from a notebook file or object as expressions, text, boxes or Cell objects (style -> form), without opening it in the front end. It is the easiest way to extract code ("Input" -> "HeldExpression") or text from notebooks in batch jobs and CI pipelines.
tools.usage:
NotebookImport["file.nb", "Input"]
NotebookImport[nb, "Input" -> "HeldExpression"]
NotebookImport[nb, "Text" -> "Text"]
NotebookImport[nb, _ -> "Cell"]

tools.name: NotebookTemplate
tools.description: Turns a notebook containing TemplateSlot cells and expressions into a template that GenerateDocument fills with data (association of slot values) to produce reports; TemplateSlot, TemplateIf and TemplateSequence markup control substitution. Use it for automated periodic reports.
tools.usage:
tpl = NotebookTemplate["template.nb"]
GenerateDocument[tpl, <|"slot1" -> val1, ...|>]
GenerateDocument[tpl, args, "report.nb"]

parameters.name: nb
parameters.description: Notebook file or object containing template slots.

parameters.name: args
parameters.description: Association of slot names to values.

tools.example:
tpl = NotebookTemplate["weekly.nb"];
GenerateDocument[tpl, <|"date" -> Today, "data" -> sales|>, "weekly-" <> DateString["ISODate"] <> ".nb"]

tools.name: CreateWindow
tools.description: Creates a new front-end window from a Notebook, DocumentNotebook, PaletteNotebook or DialogNotebook expression, returning its NotebookObject; CreatePalette is the shortcut for palettes. Use it to build tool windows with custom window options (WindowSize, WindowFloating, WindowElements, Saveable).
tools.usage:
CreateWindow[]
CreateWindow[DocumentNotebook[{cells}]]
CreateWindow[PaletteNotebook[{cells}], WindowTitle -> "Tools"]
CreatePalette[expr]
tools.example: CreatePalette[Column[{PasteButton["Plot", Defer[Plot[f[x], {x, 0, 1}]]], Button["Clear", ClearAll["Global`*"]]}], WindowTitle -> "My tools"]

tools.name: FrontEndExecute
tools.description: Sends front-end commands (FrontEndToken, FrontEnd`... packets) to the notebook front end for execution, exposing every menu command: FrontEndTokenExecute[nb, "token"] is the convenient form (e.g. "Save", "DeleteGeneratedCells", "SelectAll", "EvaluateNotebook", "PrintDialog"). Use it to automate GUI actions that have no dedicated kernel function.
tools.usage:
FrontEndExecute[FrontEndToken["token"]]
FrontEndExecute[FrontEndToken[nb, "token"]]
FrontEndTokenExecute["token"]
FrontEndTokenExecute[nb, "token", args]

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Front-end token name (see the FrontEndTokenExecute documentation for the list of tokens).

tools.name: CurrentValue
tools.description: Reads or (as an assignment target) sets front-end values: notebook/cell options, window properties, mouse and modifier-key state, colours, font sizes, and $FrontEnd-level settings. It works inside Dynamic, making it the live channel between kernel code and front-end state.
tools.usage:
CurrentValue["prop"]
CurrentValue[nb, prop]
CurrentValue[cell, {TaggingRules, "key"}]
CurrentValue[nb, WindowTitle] = "New title"
CurrentValue[$FrontEnd, {"prop"}]

tools.name: TaggingRules
tools.description: Option of notebooks and cells holding arbitrary key -> value metadata that is saved with the file; read and written via CurrentValue[nb, {TaggingRules, key}]. The standard place to persist tool settings and document metadata inside a notebook.
tools.usage:
CurrentValue[nb, {TaggingRules, "key"}]
CurrentValue[nb, {TaggingRules, "key"}] = value
SetOptions[nb, TaggingRules -> {"author" -> "me"}]

tools.name: StyleDefinitions
tools.description: Notebook option giving the stylesheet (a name like "Default.nb" or a Notebook of StyleData cells) that defines cell styles; StyleData["Style"] cells inside it set per-style options. Change it to restyle a whole document or embed custom styles for portability.
tools.usage:
SetOptions[nb, StyleDefinitions -> "ReverseColor.nb"]
CreateDocument[cells, StyleDefinitions -> Notebook[{Cell[StyleData[StyleDefinitions -> "Default.nb"]], Cell[StyleData["Section"], FontColor -> Blue]}]]

tools.name: $FrontEnd
tools.description: The FrontEndObject of the current front end (Null when there is none, e.g. in plain wolframscript). Options[$FrontEnd] / CurrentValue[$FrontEnd, ...] read and set global preferences; $FrontEndSession holds session-only overrides. Test $FrontEnd =!= Null to decide between GUI and console behaviour.
tools.usage:
$FrontEnd
$FrontEndSession
CurrentValue[$FrontEnd, {"prop"}]
SetOptions[$FrontEnd, opt -> value]
tools.example:
If[$FrontEnd === Null, Print["headless"], MessageDialog["done"]]
CurrentValue[$FrontEndSession, Magnification] = 1.5
tools.notes: UsingFrontEnd[expr] starts a hidden front end from a kernel-only session so that Rasterize, NotebookOpen etc. work in scripts.

tools.name: UsingFrontEnd
tools.description: Evaluates expr with a front end available, launching a hidden front end if the kernel was started without one (wolframscript, WSTP links). Needed for Rasterize, Export of notebooks, NotebookOpen and other front-end-dependent operations in batch scripts.
tools.usage: UsingFrontEnd[expr]
tools.notes: Since Version 12 many exports rasterize without a front end, but notebook manipulation still needs one.

tools.name: NotebookFileName
tools.description: Gives the full path of the file a notebook is saved as ($Failed for unsaved notebooks); NotebookInformation returns an association of properties (file name, window title, modification state, cell count). Use them to locate data files relative to the notebook and to check unsaved state before batch operations.
tools.usage:
NotebookFileName[]
NotebookFileName[nb]
NotebookInformation[nb]

tools.name: SetSelectedNotebook
tools.description: Brings a notebook window to the front and makes it the selected notebook, so subsequent input and SelectedNotebook[] refer to it. Use it after creating windows programmatically or when driving several notebooks.
tools.usage: SetSelectedNotebook[nb]

tools.name: DocumentNotebook
tools.description: DocumentNotebook[{cells}], PaletteNotebook[{cells}] and DialogNotebook[{cells}] are notebook expressions pre-configured as an ordinary document, a palette (floating, non-editable) or a dialog; pass them to CreateWindow or NotebookPut to instantiate windows of the right kind.
tools.usage:
CreateWindow[DocumentNotebook[{TextCell["Hi", "Title"]}]]
CreateWindow[PaletteNotebook[{...}]]
CreateWindow[DialogNotebook[{...}]]

parameters.name: {cells}
parameters.description: List of Cell expressions or expressions convertible to cells.

tools.name: CellChangeTimes
tools.description: Cell option automatically recording the absolute times at which a cell was edited (a list of AbsoluteTime values); useful for auditing notebooks and, when stripping notebooks for version control, a frequent target for removal along with CellID and CellLabel. Other useful cell options: Editable, Deletable, CellOpen, CellFrame, CellMargins, InitializationCell, GeneratedCell, CellAutoOverwrite.
tools.usage:
Options[cell, CellChangeTimes]
SetOptions[cell, Editable -> False, Deletable -> False]
Cell[..., InitializationCell -> True]
Cell[..., CellOpen -> False]

parameters.name: InitializationCell
parameters.description: True: cell is evaluated when the notebook's initialization is run.

parameters.name: GeneratedCell
parameters.description: True for output cells produced by evaluation (deleted by DeleteGeneratedCells).

parameters.name: CellAutoOverwrite
parameters.description: True: cell is replaced by new output on re-evaluation.

tools.name: NotebookDynamicExpression
tools.description: Notebook option holding a Dynamic expression that is evaluated continuously while the notebook is open, e.g. to keep a WindowTitle updated or run a background watcher. DockedCells adds a fixed toolbar area at the top of the window - the standard place for custom notebook toolbars.
tools.usage:
SetOptions[nb, NotebookDynamicExpression :> Dynamic[Refresh[check[], UpdateInterval -> 5]]]
SetOptions[nb, DockedCells -> Cell[BoxData[ToBoxes[Row[{Button["Run all", NotebookEvaluate[nb]]}]]], "DockedCell"]]

parameters.name: DockedCells
parameters.description: Cell or list of cells docked at the top of the window.

tools.example: SetOptions[EvaluationNotebook[], DockedCells -> Cell[TextData[{"Report toolbar  ", Cell[BoxData[ToBoxes[Button["Export PDF", Export["out.pdf", EvaluationNotebook[]]]]]]}], "DockedCell"]]

tools.name: CellGroup
tools.description: CellGroup[{cell1, cell2, ...}] (in Cell[CellGroupData[...]] form inside notebooks) groups cells hierarchically under a heading cell with an Open/Closed state; FrontEndTokenExecute "CellGroup"/"CellUngroup" and SelectionMove with unit CellGroup operate on groups. Understanding groups is necessary when programmatically inserting sections.
tools.usage:
Cell[CellGroupData[{Cell["Section", "Section"], Cell["body", "Text"]}, Open]]
SelectionMove[nb, Next, CellGroup]
FrontEndTokenExecute[nb, "CellGroup"]

tools.name: NB
tools.description: The .nb notebook file format as handled by Import/Export/Get: a .nb file is a Notebook[{cells}, opts] expression, so Get or Import[file, "Notebook"] loads it as data that can be transformed with rules and written back with Export or Put, all without a front end. Import elements "Cells", "Plaintext" and "Text" extract content. Use it for version-control clean-up and mass edits of notebooks.
tools.usage:
nb = Get["file.nb"]
nb = Import["file.nb", "Notebook"]
Export["file2.nb", nb]
Import["file.nb", "Plaintext"]
tools.notes: Import elements for notebooks include "Cells", "Plaintext", "Text", "Notebook" and "NotebookObject".

tools.name: EvaluationCell
tools.description: Returns the CellObject of the cell currently being evaluated, the anchor for relative cell operations: NextCell/PreviousCell to reach outputs or neighbours, ParentCell for the enclosing group, SelectionMove[EvaluationCell[], ...] to position insertions right after the running cell.
tools.usage:
EvaluationCell[]
NextCell[EvaluationCell[]]
PreviousCell[cell, CellStyle -> "Section"]
ParentCell[cell]
tools.example:
SelectionMove[EvaluationCell[], After, Cell];
NotebookWrite[EvaluationNotebook[], Cell["inserted after this cell", "Text"]]

tools.name: NotebookEventActions
tools.description: Notebook (or cell) option attaching actions to keyboard and window events: "KeyDown", "ReturnKeyDown", "WindowClose", "MouseDown", etc. Use it for keyboard shortcuts in custom tools and for clean-up when a tool window is closed.
tools.usage:
SetOptions[nb, NotebookEventActions -> {"WindowClose" :> cleanup[], {"KeyDown", "r"} :> run[]}]
CreateDialog[content, NotebookEventActions -> {"ReturnKeyDown" :> DialogReturn[value]}]

tools.name: CDFDeploy
tools.description: CDFDeploy writes a notebook or Manipulate as a Computable Document Format file playable in the free Wolfram Player; more generally Export renders NotebookObjects and Notebook expressions to "PDF", "HTML", "TeX", "Text" and "Plaintext" through the front end. Use these to distribute interactive content or printable reports from generated notebooks.
tools.usage:
CDFDeploy["file.cdf", nb]
CDFDeploy["file.cdf", Manipulate[...]]
Export["report.pdf", nb]
Export["report.html", nb]
Export["report.tex", nb]
tools.notes: Requires a front end (UsingFrontEnd in scripts). PDF export paginates according to the notebook's printing options (PrintingOptions).
